heard: A giant shadow blocked up to 22% of a star's light. In 2015, citizen scientists using NASA's Kepler telescope found a weirdly behaving star. This star, later named Tabby's star, dimmed erratically by up to 22%. A normal planet like Jupiter blocks only about 1% of a star's light. To explain the massive dip, some researchers speculated we were seeing an alien megastructure. But telescopes showed the light dims differently depending on its wavelength, ruling out solid structures. Instead, a massive cloud of space dust, possibly from an evaporating exomoon, is blocking the light. This swirling dust is the true cosmic culprit casting that giant shadow.
